verdict.rationale: Grafana Cloud's Knowledge Graph generates insights that surface configuration changes alongside errors and anomalies, and Database Observability documents analyzing deployment impact. These are first-party capabilities that touch change correlation, but each is a one-line claim scoped to a specific Cloud feature, with no general release or deploy tracking documented. Provisioning and as-code version control apply to Grafana's own configuration, so they are not change tracking for the monitored system and earn no credit. Missing for 10: a general deploy/release event-tracking mechanism (such as deploy markers or annotations ingested from CI/CD), documented overlay of change events on regression graphs across services, detail on how configuration changes are detected and correlated, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can correlate regressions with deploys and configuration changes via release or change tracking

citations.quote: It continuously generates insights that highlight saturation, errors, anomalies, failures, and configuration changes
troubleshoot high error rates, analyze deployment impact
